title: Exchange reduces to the canonical invertible-order torsion kernels
statement: Let K be a field, f:X to Spec K finite type, S and T arbitrary K-schemes and g:T to S qcqs over K. Put X'=X times_K S and Y=X' times_S T. Let F be an abelian etale sheaf on T whose geometric stalk elements are killed by positive integers invertible in K [def-kun-torsion-invertible]. Suppose the canonical unbounded exchange for this square on F[n][0], where F[n]=ker(n id F), is invertible for every positive n invertible in K. Then the same exchange on F[0] is invertible [def-kun-unbounded-exchange].

source.place: Tag 0F1I, lemma-punctual-base-change, degree-zero and bounded-exponent reductions; Tag 073E, filtered colimits

proof.text: Positive invertible orders form a filtered category under divisibility: 1 is an index and nm is a common upper bound. The stalk hypothesis gives torsion stalks, hence F is torsion. The canonical map from the colimit of the kernels F[n] to F is an isomorphism.

Apply filtered-colimit exchange to the kernel diagram using the assumed component isomorphisms. Transport its component at the colimit along the canonical comparison isomorphism to its component at F by naturality.
